title: Dates set for coroner's inquest into 2019 death at Regional Psychiatric Centre
subtitle: The inquest into the death of 32-year-old Benjamin Toutsaint is scheduled for March 21 to 25 in Saskatoon.
article: The Saskatchewan Coroners Service has announced the dates for the inquest into the death of 32-year-old Benjamin Toutsaint at the Regional Psychiatric Centre in Saskatoon in 2019.
The inquest is scheduled for March 21 to 25 at the Saskatoon Inn and Conference Centre, with Saskatoon lawyer Brent Gough as the presiding coroner.
Toutsaint was found unresponsive in his cell at the federal correctional facility on May 18, 2019. Medical staff responded and life-saving attempts were unsuccessful.
He began serving a sentence of two years and four days for assault in October 2018, a previous media release from the CSC said.

Inquests are a public fact-finding - not fault-finding - process that establishes who died, when and how. The process may also highlight dangerous conditions or practices, and the six-member jury can make non-binding recommendations.

The chief coroner, under the provincial Coroners Act, is to hold an inquest into the death of anyone who dies in custody, unless they are satisfied the death was due entirely to natural causes and was not preventable.
